question: Related Questions Q. The situation is: my grandfather gave my father agricultural land and village property.my father is the only son and has five sisters. The peoperty is 6 acres of land and a house. As per village traditions, my grand father did not give any share to his daughters. My grand father died in 2000 and my father becomes owner of property and he added 10 more acres to the property from his earnings. Property is now being transferred to me as sole male heir, i have two sisters as well. Now I don't want to do the same and infact I wish to reverse what my grand father and the my father has done. I wish to give my phuphoos (my father's sisters their share which should have been given by my grand father) and to my sisters as per shariah as I don't want to take this burdon to next world. 1.my mother is dead I have two sisters. 2.My father has five sisters out of which one has died. 3.my grand mother is alive but not in senses and bed ridden (very ill) My question is: 1.how can I rightfully do this? give my phuphoos (my father's sisters) and then remaining among myself and my sisters. 2.Am I obligated to correct my grandfather's wrong act of not giving share to daughters? 2.my grandfather died in 2000 so the price of land at that time will be used to do shares? Can we use price of property in year 2000 as that was the time for doing the sahres. I am planning to sell everything and then do the shares. Assume price of one acre as 1,000,000 in 2007 price of one acre in year 2000 was 500,000. grand father left 6 acres father added 10 more Thanks in advance for guidence. 2057 views Q. Asalam alaikum, My eleder brother expired two years ago leaving behind a wife and a minor child. After some period of time recently, the widow (wife of deceased) got remarried. In this point of view we went to Darul Ifta in Hyderabad to know the Sharia Law for the child custody in such situations. They gave us saying that the Child if female shall be with mother and if male then after her remarriage the child until the age of 7 should be with the maternal grandmother if she is alive and later after 7 to the paternal grandparents if she is not alive then the custody shall be for the paternal grand parents. Now the problem is we have been seeking from the widow the custody but they are reluctant to give when we show them the fatwa they told us to keep it aside and they want to have the share from the property (the share of the widow). we have no problem in giving the share we evaluated as be the sharia law and gave the figure how much will it be and later they keep on delaying things with the intention to avoid the cutodial issue of the child. Until now the issue is pending so far we havent seek any assistance from the court. we would like to seek your kind assistance is doing the rightful. Please guide us, and show us path to safegaurd the childs mental conditions as t he mother (widow) took the child with her to his new husband. Guide us how can we enforce the sharia law, the fatwa issued by Darul Ifta. 1992 views Q. Inheritance and Loan 2183 views Q. I would appreciate an answer to the below question. This question is about the definition of will(wasiat) in the shareia. My brother died last year leaving behind a wife, a Son and adopted Daugther.Few clarifications before the question: 1.He did not have child from his first wife and they both adopted a girl as adopted child. This adopted child is a daughter of my other brother and she was 1-1/2 year old when adopted. 2.He had a 2nd marriage couple of years ago and from this 2nd wife ,Allah blessed him with a boy baby. 3.Before the birth of the Son, his first wife died. 4.He himself left for the next world when the Son was just two month old. 5.Our parents are alive and living with us 6.Adopted daughter is 11 years of age now It is clear from the Islamic law of inheritance that following are the heirs: 1.Wife 2.Son 3.His father 4.His Mother And it is also known that the adopted kid will not get any share from the things left by the brother. As brother was working in a company where every year one document is to be signed describing the persons who will be considered heirs to distribute the provident fund incase of employ's death. This document was signed after the death of his first wife and before the birth of the Son from the 2nd wife. He mentioned in the document that my provident fund is distributed to my wife and the adopted kid with out describing the proportion. Question: Can we consider this document as will (wasiah) and if this is wasiah, would the adopted kid have a portion and if yes. What should be this portion? Will this portion amount should be taken out from the total asset and rest is distributed to legal heirs? I would appreciate your valued inputs to this request. 1870 views Q. i have one daughter and no son. i have one brother with no child and 2 sisters married. i want to know after my demise how will my property would be shared? if my daughter inherits half of my property then what will happen to my other half property. if i want to give her all my wealth, can i gift her all my property in my lifetime. plz elaborate. 1790 views Q. inheritance and making will for widowed daughter in law and granddaughter. 1931 views Q. Assalaam Alaikum, A Man dies leaving behind a wife and two daughters from the wife.He has left behind him some self aquired property. After his death , his brother's sons ( bhatijay ) have demanded a share from the property,even though their father, i.e.; the deceased man's brother died much before him. Earlier, during the deceased man's lifetime, these nephews demanded a share in his property claiming joint ownership of the business between their father and the deceased man.However, the same was rejected in a court of law , by virtue of proofs,evidences and records. Is this claim , now,by the nephews, allowed?,even after the death of their father? Are the nephews entitled to any share of the inheritance from their uncle's ( deceased man )property in the absence of their father? The deceased man did not have any liking for them during his lifetime as they embroiled him in unnecessary and unwanted legal controversies. Your answer in this regard shall be highly appreciated. 1743 views
answer: Transactions & Dealings >> Inheritance & Will Question ID: 31926 Country: United Kingdom Title: Dividing Inheritance Question: One of my friends dad passed away and they want to divide the inheritance between them the dad have 3 Sons,2 Daughters and 1 Son from divorced wife who left the son with her husband and left forever The dad have properties worth of 80 Hundred housand Rupees and 4 Hundred Thousand Rupees (money)so please could you please explain the dividing of this on the number of people mentioned on top. Answer ID: 31926 Posted on: Aug 30, 2020 Bismillah hir-Rahman nir-Rahim ! (Fatwa: 937/L=348/TL=1432) In the question mentioned above, if the son of the divorced wife of your friend's father is the son of your friend's father, (he will get his share). If the parents of deceased or any wife (that is not divorcee) is not alive at the time of his death, then all the property of the deceased father shall be divided into 10 shares out of which each son shall get 2-2 shares and 1-1 share to each daughter, as per the following details: Detail: Son: 4x2 = 8 Daughter: 2x1 = 2 Total: 10 Shares Note: If the son of divorced wife is from other husband (other than your friend’s father) then explain it and submit the question again. Allah (Subhana Wa Ta'ala) knows Best Darul Ifta, Darul Uloom Deoband, India
